issues.failure_explanation: The proof applies Lemma lem4 with X = |s_{\tau_i}|^2|r_{\tau_i}|^2 = f(\tau_i) and Y = 1/\|S_\tau A_\tau\|_2^2 to write E(XY) = E[X\,E(Y|X)], then silently replaces E(Y|X) with E(Y|\tau_i). Since \sigma(X) \subseteq \sigma(\tau_i) and f need not be injective (two rows j \ne j' can satisfy |s_j|^2|r_j|^2 = |s_{j'}|^2|r_{j'}|^2), one has E(Y|X) = E[E(Y|\tau_i)|X] \ne E(Y|\tau_i) in general. The conclusion of the lemma is correct but this inference is invalid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the two-step conditioning with a direct tower-property argument: E[f(\tau_i)Y] = E[E[f(\tau_i)Y \mid \tau_i]] = E[f(\tau_i)\,E[Y \mid \tau_i]], yielding the same summation over j without invoking E(Y|X) = E(Y|\tau_i).
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem6's proof contains an invalid conditional-expectation step. The lemma's conclusion is nonetheless correct and feeds correctly into Theorem convRBSK once the gap is closed.
issues.title: Incorrect conditional-expectation identity in Lemma lem6 proof
issues.why_classification: The lemma's conclusion is correct and the fix replaces a single inference line with a standard tower-property application; every downstream guarantee survives unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: When d_\tau = rank(A_\tau) = d = rank(A), the subspace \mathcal{W}_\tau is {0}, so W_\tau is an n x 0 matrix and W_\tau^T A^T D^2 A W_\tau is a 0 x 0 matrix. The quantity \lambda_min of a 0 x 0 matrix is undefined. Consequently \xi = \min_{\tau} \xi_\tau in Theorem convRBSK (and the analogous quantities in the dependent results) is ill-defined whenever a draw \tau with positive probability satisfies d_\tau = d.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define \xi_\tau = +\infty (or 1) when d_\tau = d, since x^{(k+1)} = x_\star and the rate bound is trivially satisfied; equivalently, take the minimum only over draws with d_\tau < d.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence-rate bound formulas in Theorem convRBSK, Corollary convRBSK_relaxed, Theorem convRBSK_relaxed_pave, and Theorem convRBSK_sharper are ill-defined whenever some batch-sampling draw yields a block whose row rank equals rank(A). (In that case the iteration converges in one step but the rate expression is still undefined.)
issues.title: \xi_\tau ill-defined when d_\tau = d (degenerate zero-dimensional W_\tau)
issues.why_classification: A standard convention for the degenerate 0 x 0 case or an explicit exclusion restores well-definedness. No bound's value changes in non-degenerate cases and no guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem6 defines \beta^S_{i,j} as the max of \|S_\tau A_\tau\|_2^2 over draws \tau with \tau_i = j, where A_\tau has q rows including repeats when |T_{I(j)}| < q. The proof of Theorem convRBSK_relaxed_pave claims \beta^S_{i,j} = \|S_{T_{I(j)}} A_{T_{I(j)}}\|_2^2, ignoring the strict increase in \|S_\tau A_\tau\|_2^2 caused by repeated row indices. When some block T_t has |T_t| < q, the actual \beta^S_{i,j} exceeds \|S_{T_{I(j)}} A_{T_{I(j)}}\|_2^2 (e.g., for T = {\{1\}}, q = 2 one has \beta^S_{i,1} = 2\|s_1 a_1\|^2 but \|S_{T_1} A_{T_1}\|^2 = \|s_1 a_1\|^2). Hence B_S is understated, B_S^{-1} is overstated, and the claimed matrix inequality D^2 \succeq S^T B_S^{-1} \widehat{P} S used to derive the rate bound is not established. The proof's claim B_{S;i} = B_S for all i likewise fails to match Lemma lem6's B_{S;i}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either (a) redefine B_S with entries equal to the correct \beta^S_{i,j} from Lemma lem6 that account for repeated row indices (yielding a weaker but valid bound with the same formulaic structure), or (b) add the hypothesis |T_t| = q for all t so the current identification is correct.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence-rate bound in Theorem convRBSK_relaxed_pave is unestablished whenever row-paving blocks have unequal sizes (|T_t| < q for some t). The sharpness comparison in Remark remark:relaxTwo and the experimental comparisons using this bound are correspondingly unreliable.
issues.title: Incorrect identification of \beta^S_{i,j} with block norm in Theorem convRBSK_relaxed_pave
issues.why_classification: The repair requires either redefining B_S (changing the bound's numerical value and weakening the advertised sharpness comparison) or restricting the hypothesis to equal-size blocks (narrowing scope). A recognizably comparable linear-convergence bound survives but more than a routine local fix is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem's hypothesis states cov(\xi_{\tau^{(k-1)}}, \|x^{(k)}-x_\star\|_2) \geq 0 (non-squared norm), but the proof applies Lemma lem5 with y_i = \|x^{(k,i)}-x_\star\|_2^2 (squared norm) in the key inequality (thm4Eq5). Lemma lem5 requires the sample covariance of \xi and \|x^{(k)}-x_\star\|_2^2 to be non-negative. cov(\xi, \|x-x_\star\|_2) \geq 0 does not imply cov(\xi, \|x-x_\star\|_2^2) \geq 0 in general (e.g., \xi positively correlated with the norm but negatively correlated with its square). The proof therefore invokes Lemma lem5 outside its hypotheses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the hypothesis from cov(\xi_{\tau^{(k-1)}}, \|x^{(k)}-x_\star\|_2) \geq 0 to cov(\xi_{\tau^{(k-1)}}, \|x^{(k)}-x_\star\|_2^2) \geq 0, matching what Lemma lem5 requires.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence-rate bound in Theorem convRBSK_sharper is unestablished because its stated hypothesis is insufficient for the proof's key covariance step.
issues.title: Covariance hypothesis stated for unsquared norm while proof needs squared norm
issues.why_classification: A one-line change to the hypothesis restores the proof step's validity with no change to the conclusion, rate, or method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Taking expectation on both sides of (\ref{thm4Eq8}) leads to the sharper estimate (\ref{thm4Eq2}).

issues.failure_explanation: The quantity E(\|x^{(k+1)}-x_\star\|_2^2) is deterministic (a property of the algorithm's distribution). Stating that it holds 'with probability at least 1-\delta' is meaningless. The proof obtains (thm4Eq8) with probability \geq 1-\delta (via Hoeffding on the sample mean of \xi) and then claims that 'taking expectation on both sides' yields (thm4Eq2). But an inequality holding only on an event of probability 1-\delta cannot be converted to an expectation inequality by taking expectations: E[LHS] \leq E[RHS] does not follow from LHS \leq RHS holding with probability 1-\delta. Moreover, the concentration step is unnecessary and adds an \epsilon slack that weakens the bound: a direct argument applying the population covariance condition cov(\xi_\tau, \|x^{(k)}-x_\star\|_2^2) \geq 0 to (thm1Eq3) after taking full expectations yields the strictly sharper deterministic bound E(\|x^{(k+1)}-x_\star\|_2^2) \leq (1 - E[\xi_\tau]) E(\|x^{(k)}-x_\star\|_2^2).

failure_location.quote: then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the mean squared error satisfies

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the concentration-based argument with a direct expectation argument: take full expectations of (thm1Eq3) and use the population covariance condition cov(\xi_\tau, \|x^{(k)}-x_\star\|_2^2) \geq 0 to obtain the deterministic bound E(\|x^{(k+1)}-x_\star\|_2^2) \leq (1 - E[\xi_\tau]) E(\|x^{(k)}-x_\star\|_2^2), removing the concentration step, probability qualifier, and \epsilon slack.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence-rate bound in Theorem convRBSK_sharper is unestablished as stated. The paper's advertised use of concentration inequalities to derive expected linear convergence rate bounds does not deliver a valid deterministic bound on the mean squared error.
issues.title: Concentration step yields nonsensical probability qualifier on deterministic MSE bound
issues.why_classification: The repair requires restructuring the proof (replacing the concentration argument with a direct expectation argument) and restating the conclusion (deterministic bound without probability qualifier and without \epsilon). The covariance-based improvement over the min_\tau bound and the linear convergence guarantee survive and are strengthened, but the proof architecture within this theorem must be replaced.
